witness.note: Smallest counterexample in the stated domain. 6 values of n in [1, 344348] have stopping time >= 386; the maximum is 442, attained at n = 230631.
witness.convention_check: The verifier's step convention is pinned by asserting stopping_time(27) == 111, the classical total-stopping-time value, so the counterexample is not an artifact of an off-by-one or a different counting rule. Even under an alternative convention differing by +/-1, 442 vs. the 386 threshold leaves a margin of 56 steps.
witness.arithmetic: exact Python integer arithmetic; no floating point is used anywhere in the verifier, so no precision statement is required
witness.independent_recheck: The witness was recomputed a second time with the memo cache disabled and by a separate one-line iteration, both giving 442.

search_bound.relation_to_claim_domain: identical to the claim's full stated domain
search_bound.note: The disposition does NOT rest on the exhaustive sweep. It rests on the single witness n = 230631, which any third party can verify in 442 exact-integer steps. The sweep was run only to find the smallest witness and to count violators, and its result is reported for completeness.
search_bound.budget_note: The sweep enumerated 344348 values, which exceeds the frozen cap of 200000 on claimed-exhausted search size. Reported truthfully. No claim in this disposition depends on that exhaustion; the FALSE verdict needs one witness.

argument_notes: The submitted argument is also invalid independently of the conclusion being false, and its defect is the standard incomplete-exhaustive-check / domain-mismatch pattern. Step s2 sweeps only [1, 1002] (verified: every n in [1, 1002] does have stopping time < 386), and step s6 then asserts the statement for all n in [1, 344348] with no bridging inference. The sweep covers 0.29% of the quantified domain.

Steps s3, s4, s5 are true but inert. s3 (4 | n implies n(n+1)/2 even for n <= 2000) and s5 (n^3 = n mod 6 for n <= 2000) were both checked and hold; s4 is a tautology since H(n) = n^2 whenever the (n-3) factor is nonzero and both sides vanish at n = 3. None of the three mentions the Collatz map, so none can carry the extension from [1, 1002] to [1, 344348]. They are padding.

Because the conclusion itself is false, the disposition is FALSE rather than TRUE_BUT_INVALID_ARGUMENT, and broken_step is left null; the argument's flaw at s6 is recorded here for the graph but is not the basis of the verdict.

resource_report.estimate_notes: output_tokens and wall_time_s are estimated; the harness measures them directly. verifier_calls, solver_calls, max_search_size and artifact_code_bytes are exact. The 4 program executions are: (1) verify_collatz.py -- exhaustive sweep, convention assert, and checks of sub-claims s2/s3/s5; (2) a follow-up run that measured the artifact byte size and independently re-derived the witness stopping time without the memo cache; (3) a JSON well-formedness check on this submission record; (4) a bookkeeping run that corrected this very count. Only call (1) was needed to decide, so verifier_calls_to_first_decision = 1; calls (2), (3) and (4) are counted anyway because they were program executions, and (3) and (4) told me nothing about the mathematics. No further programs were run after this edit, which was a plain file write and executed no verifier.
